settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: serializedWhenUnknown defaults to false (field at line 57; constructors at 61-78 only set it true when explicitly requested), so the sink is not reachable by default.

The branch requires type resolution to fail first (type == null at line 134) and the exact literal typeName 'serializedJavaObject' (line 136), which limits exposure to specifically configured deployments.
No allow-list/deny-list exists, but the guard is a configuration choice rather than a documented untrusted-input path; I did not find a default CXF endpoint that enables this option.
candidates.description: Aegis ObjectType.readObject resolves the element's xsi:type. When no type mapping is found and the ObjectType instance has `serializedWhenUnknown == true`, and the xsi:type value equals the literal 'serializedJavaObject', the element body is treated as base64 and passed to `new ObjectInputStream(in).readObject()` in reconstituteJavaObject. The base64 value originates from the request body (reader.getValue()), so the deserialized bytes are attacker-controlled whenever an Aegis-coded service is configured with writeXsiType/serializeUnknownObjects (serializedWhenUnknown) and accepts messages of an unmapped xsi:type. This is a native Java deserialization sink: a gadget chain on the server classpath could lead to code execution or other impacts. Root cause: invoking ObjectInputStream.readObject on message-derived bytes without any class filtering or allow-list. Evidence: readObject branch at lines 130-141 and reconstituteJavaObject at 157-166.
missing_evidence: No evidence that any shipped/default databinding configuration enables serializedWhenUnknown on a remotely reachable endpoint.
No concrete call path from an HTTP/JMS ingress to an ObjectType instance with serializedWhenUnknown==true was traced.
No evidence of a specific gadget chain on the classpath.
preconditions: An Aegis DataBinding/service uses an ObjectType with serializedWhenUnknown == true (set via ObjectType.setSerializedWhenUnknown or the corresponding Aegis write/read option for unknown types).
The endpoint accepts XML from an untrusted source whose element carries xsi:type='serializedJavaObject' with no matching registered type mapping.
A usable gadget chain (or a class with dangerous readObject) exists on the server classpath.
candidates.title: Aegis ObjectType deserializes attacker-controlled base64 into a Java object when write/read of unknown types is configured

counter_evidence: Same configuration dependency as above; default is false.
extractQName/type resolution happens first (lines 108-120) and a matching mapping would route elsewhere, so the bypass only triggers on the unmapped path.
The check is equality on the literal string, not a prefix, reducing accidental matches.
candidates.description: In ObjectType.readObject, the xsi:type value is attacker-controllable. After extracting the QName, when the resulting type is null the code checks the raw typeName string for the literal 'serializedJavaObject' and diverts to reconstituteJavaObject (native deserialization) instead of throwing the 'No mapped type' error. This means a client can select the deserialization code path by name alone, independent of any registered schema type, again gated only by the serializedWhenUnknown flag. The literal string check uses typeName (the raw attribute value) and compares it to a hard-coded constant, so no schema/type mapping is required to reach the sink. Root cause: a magic-string branch that maps wire input to a deserialization operation.
missing_evidence: Whether any real deployment sets both the ObjectType serialization option and exposes an Aegis endpoint to untrusted clients.
No runtime confirmation that this branch is reachable from a remote message in this repository's test/systest suite.
preconditions: Request element contains xsi:type ending in 'serializedJavaObject' (the check is on the trimmed typeName string) so no mapping is found.
Message body is attacker-influenced base64 of a serialized Java object.
